stem.text: A rock R of mass $1.0 \times 10^{27}\,\text{kg}$ is a large distance from a star S and is travelling at a speed of $1.0 \times 10^{4}\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. The star has mass $1.0 \times 10^{30}\,\text{kg}$. The rock travels around the star on the path shown so that it reverses its direction of motion and, when finally again a large distance from the star, has the same speed as initially.

stem.alt: Curved path of a rock around a star. The rock is labelled R at the top of the path and the star is labelled S. A horizontal arrow labelled X points left from the star. Labels give the speed and mass of the rock at the top and bottom of the path and the mass of the star.

A.text: The change in the momentum of S is in the direction of arrow X.

B.text: The change in the velocity of S is approximately $20\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.

C.text: The magnitude of the change of momentum of R is $10^{3}$ times greater than the magnitude of the change of momentum of S.

D.text: The momentum of R does not change.
